questions.question: Which statement about iron ore distribution in India is INCORRECT?

options.text: Only hematite iron ore is found in India

__

• **Odisha** is one of the largest producers of iron ore in India, and it has major iron ore belts located in **Sundargarh and Mayurbhanj**. Statement 2 is correct.
 
• **India** has significant iron ore reserves and is considered to hold a major position in Asia in terms of iron ore production. Statement 3 is correct.
 
• Over **90%** of India's iron ore reserves are concentrated in **Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, and Goa**. These states contribute the majority of iron ore production. Statement 4 is correct.

__
 
• **Types of Iron Ore Found in India:**

 
 
• **Hematite:** Known as "Red Ore," it is rich in iron content and widely distributed in Odisha, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh.
 
• **Magnetite:** Known as "Black Ore," it has a higher iron content than hematite and is primarily found in Karnataka and Goa.
 
 
 
• **Key Iron Ore Regions in India:**
 
 
• **Odisha:** Major belts include **Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, and Sundargarh**. Odisha contributes significantly to India's iron ore exports.
 
• **Jharkhand:** Prominent regions include **Singhbhum district**, which is rich in hematite deposits.
 
• **Chhattisgarh:** Known for its **Bailadila region**, which has high-quality iron ore reserves.
 
• **Karnataka:** The **Bellary-Hospet region** is a notable area for magnetite production.
 
• **Goa:** The state is known for its high-grade magnetite deposits and is a key exporter of iron ore.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Iron Ore:**
 
 
• Iron ore is a key raw material for the **steel industry**, which is essential for infrastructure development and industrial growth.
 
• India is the second-largest producer of steel globally, and iron ore plays a vital role in this achievement.
 
• The export of iron ore contributes significantly to India's **foreign exchange earnings**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Iron Ore Mining:**
 
 
• **Environmental concerns:** Mining activities often lead to deforestation and soil erosion.
 
• **Regulatory hurdles:** Licensing and permissions for mining can be complex and time-consuming.
 
• **Global market fluctuation:** The demand and price of iron ore depend on international market dynamics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Odisha:** This state accounts for **over 50%** of India's iron ore production, with its mines being a major contributor to exports.
 
• **Steel Industry:** Iron ore is crucial for the steel industry, which forms the backbone of India's construction and manufacturing sectors.
 
• **Iron Ore Exports:** India exports iron ore primarily to **China, Japan, and South Korea**, making it a significant player in the global market.
 
• **Reserves:** India has estimated iron ore reserves of approximately **23 billion tonnes**, ensuring long-term availability for industrial use.

questions.question: Which State/UT recorded the lowest sex ratio as per Census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Daman and Diu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Census 2011**, **Daman and Diu** recorded the lowest sex ratio in India, with only **618 females per 1000 males**.
 
• The sex ratio is a crucial demographic indicator that reflects the number of females per 1000 males in a region, and it plays a significant role in understanding the gender dynamics of a population.
 
• **Daman and Diu**, being a small Union Territory, faced challenges like **gender-based discrimination and socio-economic issues**, which contributed to its low sex ratio.
 
• Other states/UTs with low sex ratios include **Haryana (879 females per 1000 males)** and **Punjab (895 females per 1000 males)**, but they have better ratios compared to Daman and Diu.
 
• Efforts like **Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao** were launched by the Indian government to address declining sex ratios and promote gender equality in various regions, including those with historically low sex ratios.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sex Ratio in India**:

 
 
• The **sex ratio** is defined as the number of females per 1000 males in a given population, and it is a vital social indicator to measure the equality of genders in a society.
 
• The overall sex ratio of India, as per Census 2011, was **940 females per 1000 males**.
 
• Kerala recorded the highest sex ratio with **1084 females per 1000 males**, showcasing better gender equity.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Sex Ratio**:
 
 
• Key factors influencing low sex ratios include **female infanticide, gender-based abortions, societal preferences for male children**, and lack of education and awareness.
 
• Socio-economic conditions and cultural practices also contribute to the disparity in gender ratios.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives**:
 
 
• **Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao**: Launched in **2015**, this scheme aims to address the declining child sex ratio and empower the girl child through education and awareness.

questions.question: Which title was commonly adopted by Kushana rulers to reflect divine lineage?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Kushana rulers adopted the title **Devaputra**, which translates to "**Son of God**." This title reflected their divine lineage and their claim to semi-divine status.
 
• The Kushanas were originally a branch of the Yuezhi, a nomadic group from Central Asia, and their rule spanned parts of **India, Central Asia, and China** during the 1st to 3rd centuries CE.
 
• The adoption of the title "Devaputra" was influenced by their interaction with **Hellenistic, Indian, and Central Asian cultures**. It emphasized their divine right to rule.
 
• One of the most notable Kushana rulers, **Kanishka I**, extensively used this title. His reign is considered a golden age for cultural and economic prosperity in the empire.
 
• By claiming the title "Devaputra," the Kushanas sought to legitimize their rule over a culturally diverse empire and integrate religious and cultural traditions such as **Buddhism, Hinduism, and Zoroastrianism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kushana Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Kushanas ruled from approximately the **1st to the 3rd century CE** and were instrumental in promoting trade along the **Silk Route**.
 
• Their empire included regions of modern-day **Afghanistan, Pakistan, northern India, and Central Asia**.
 
• Their coins and inscriptions provide evidence of their vast empire and their adoption of multiple religions, including **Buddhism, Hinduism, and Zoroastrianism**.
 
 
 
• **Other Titles Used by Kushana Rulers:**
 
 
• **Rajadhiraja:** This title means "King of Kings." While important in Indian history, it was not commonly adopted by the Kushanas.
 
• **Chakravartin:** This term means "Universal Monarch" and denotes a ruler who has control over the entire world or a large part of it. It was used in Indian history but not specifically emphasized by the Kushanas.
 
• **Maharajadhiraja:** Translated as "Great King of Kings," it was a common title for powerful Indian rulers but not unique to the Kushanas.
 
 
 
• **Religious Contributions of the Kushanas:**
 
 
• The Kushanas played a significant role in the spread of **Buddhism**. They supported Buddhist monasteries and were patrons of Buddhist art and architecture.
 
• Kanishka I, a prominent ruler, convened the **Fourth Buddhist Council** in Kashmir, which was instrumental in spreading Buddhism to Central and East Asia.
 
• The Gandhara and Mathura schools of art flourished under their patronage, blending **Hellenistic and Indian artistic traditions**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Kushanas:**
 
 
• The Kushanas were pivotal in connecting the Indian subcontinent with **Central Asia and the Mediterranean** through trade, cultural exchange, and the Silk Route.
 
• Their coins and inscriptions, especially in Greek, Kharosthi, and Brahmi scripts, highlight the multicultural aspect of their empire.
 
• Their contributions to art, religion, and trade left a lasting impact on Indian and world history.

questions.question: Article 263 of the Constitution primarily provides for:

__
 
• **Article 263** of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment of an **Inter-State Council** to facilitate coordination between states and the central government.
 
• The primary purpose of the council is to act as a platform for **discussions on policies and matters of common interest**, including resolving disputes between states.
 
• The **Inter-State Council** was established by the President of India under the powers vested in Article 263. It was first constituted in **1990** by then Prime Minister **Vishwanath Pratap Singh**.
 
• According to Article 263, the council can inquire into disputes, investigate issues, and provide recommendations to ensure harmony between states and the Union.
 
• The council consists of the **Prime Minister as the Chairman**, Union Ministers, Chief Ministers of States, and Administrators of Union Territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 263 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Article 263 deals with the **administrative relations between the Union and the states**.
 
• It empowers the President to create an **Inter-State Council** whenever it appears to be necessary for the better coordination of policies and actions.
 
• The council’s functions are advisory, and its recommendations are not binding.
 
• It can also investigate matters of inter-state interest or disputes between states and suggest ways to resolve them.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Inter-State Council:**
 
 
• Discussion on matters of common interest among states and Union.
 
• Investigation into disputes between states or the Union and states.
 
• Recommendation of policies to strengthen the federal structure.
 
• Promotion of cooperation and coordination between states and the Union government.
 
 
 
• **Zonal Councils:**
 
 
• While the Inter-State Council is mentioned in Article 263, **Zonal Councils** are statutorily created under the **States Reorganization Act of 1956**.
 
• Each Zonal Council covers a specific zone of states in India and addresses regional issues such as security, infrastructure, and economic development.
 
• There are five Zonal Councils: **Central, Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western**.
 
 
 
• **Emergency Provisions:**
 
 
• Emergency provisions are laid out in **Articles 352 to 360** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These provisions allow the President to impose a state of emergency in cases of war, external aggression, armed rebellion, or financial instability.
 
• Emergency provisions do not fall under Article 263 and are unrelated to the Inter-State Council.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Distinction:**

 
 
• The **Inter-State Council** is a constitutional body established under Article 263, whereas **Zonal Councils** are statutory bodies created under the States Reorganization Act.
 
 
 
• **Historical Aspect:**
 
 
• The first meeting of the Inter-State Council was held in **1990**, and it has played a significant role in fostering cooperative federalism in India.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• By fostering dialogue among states and the Union, the council helps resolve inter-state disputes and promotes better governance.

questions.question: Which ISRO mission first reported evidence of lunar hydration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandrayaan-1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandrayaan-1**, India’s first lunar probe, was launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on **22 October 2008**.
 
• The mission provided the first conclusive evidence of the presence of **water molecules (lunar hydration)** on the Moon's surface.
 
• The **Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3)**, an instrument onboard Chandrayaan-1 developed by NASA, detected **hydroxyl and water molecules** in the polar regions of the Moon.
 
• This discovery was groundbreaking, as it changed the understanding of the Moon, which was previously thought to be completely dry.
 
• The mission contributed significantly to lunar research and paved the way for future exploration missions, including Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chandrayaan-1:**

 
 
• Launched using the **PSLV-C11 rocket** from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.
 
• It was a **polar orbiting mission** with a mission life of 312 days.
 
• The spacecraft carried 11 scientific instruments, including the Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3), Terrain Mapping Camera (TMC), and Lunar Laser Ranging Instrument (LLRI).
 
• The mission also discovered **magnesium, aluminum, and silicon** on the Moon, along with water molecules.
 
• Chandrayaan-1 made over 3,400 orbits around the Moon before the mission officially ended on **29 August 2009**.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan-2:**
 
 
• Launched on **22 July 2019**, Chandrayaan-2 was India’s second lunar exploration mission.
 
• The mission consisted of an orbiter, lander (Vikram), and rover (Pragyan), aiming to explore the Moon’s south polar region.
 
• The lander, however, lost communication during its descent, but the orbiter continues to study the Moon.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan-3:**
 
 
• Launched on **14 July 2023**, Chandrayaan-3 is India’s third lunar mission.
 
• It consists of a lander and rover to demonstrate soft landing capabilities on the Moon.
 
• The mission aims to enhance the understanding of the Moon’s composition and geology.
 
 
 
• **Water on the Moon:**
 
 
• The presence of water molecules was confirmed in the **Moon’s polar regions**, primarily in permanently shadowed craters.
 
• Water on the Moon could potentially support future lunar exploration and habitation, providing resources for drinking water and fuel production.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Moon Mineralogy Mapper (M3):**

 
 
• Developed by NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), M3 was instrumental in detecting water molecules on the Moon.
 
• It used reflected sunlight to identify minerals and molecules on the Moon’s surface.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Lunar Hydration:**
 
 
• The discovery of water molecules challenged the earlier belief that the Moon was completely dry.
 
• This finding has significant implications for future lunar exploration and the potential for establishing lunar bases.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Both the President and Governor possess pardon powers under Article 72.

2. The Governor cannot grant pardon in death sentence cases.

Which is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 72** of the **Indian Constitution** empowers the **President of India** to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit, or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offense, particularly in cases involving **death sentences, court-martial offenses, and Union law violations**. *Hence, Statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 161** of the Constitution grants similar powers to the **Governor** of a state; however, the Governor's powers are limited compared to the President's and do not extend to **death sentence cases**. *Hence, Statement 2 is correct.*
 
• The Governor can pardon, remit, or commute sentences for offenses against laws that fall under the jurisdiction of the state but cannot grant pardons in cases of **death sentences**; this is exclusively the President's domain under Article 72.
 
• The distinction between the powers of the President and the Governor lies in the extent of their jurisdiction, particularly in cases involving **death sentences** and court-martial offenses.
 
• The **pardon powers** of the President and Governor are an important aspect of the **judicial review** and ensure that the executive has an opportunity to rectify judicial errors or provide relief in exceptional cases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pardon Powers of the President:**

 
 
• Under **Article 72**, the President has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment and to suspend, remit, or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offense.
 
• This power is applicable in cases where the punishment is by a court-martial, an offense against Union laws, or a death sentence.
 
• The President's power to pardon is not subject to judicial review except in cases of arbitrariness, malafide intent, or extraneous considerations.
 
 
 
• **Pardon Powers of the Governor:**
 
 
• Under **Article 161**, the Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment or suspend, remit, or commute the sentence of a person convicted under state laws.
 
• The Governor does not have the power to grant pardon in cases of **death sentences**; this power exclusively lies with the President under Article 72.
 
 
 
• **Difference between President and Governor's Pardon Powers:**
 
 
• The President's powers extend to offenses under Union laws, court-martial cases, and death sentences, while the Governor's powers are limited to offenses under state laws only.
 
• The Governor cannot interfere in cases involving death sentences or court-martial offenses.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review of Pardon Powers:**
 
 
• Although the pardon powers of the President and the Governor are discretionary, they are subject to **judicial review** if exercised arbitrarily or irrationally.
 
• The Supreme Court of India has ruled that the exercise of clemency powers must adhere to the principles of **natural justice** and fairness.
